title: EDUCATION: The Iron Law of AI Change in Schools
author: Paul Matthews
summary: Paul Matthews illustrates AI's disruptive effect on schools through an extended fable of two schools -- Geneva and Broadfields -- facing a heatwave. Geneva responds systematically while Broadfields relies on ad hoc reactions. The fable establishes a core principle: technology change, like a heatwave, doesn't wait for readiness. Matthews catalogues observable AI-driven changes already in schools: students outsourcing thinking, routine admin automated in minutes, young people turning to AI for life advice, and big tech harvesting more personal data. From this he derives Matthews' Law: if AI change in an organisation is not deliberate, it is accidental. Schools that do not actively shape their AI trajectory through vision, mission, and values will be shaped by chance and happenstance instead. Matthews frames the core choice as identity-driven change versus being swept along by the stream of unconsciousness, and concludes that while change is not optional, good change is possible.
points: Matthews' Law: if AI change in your organisation is not deliberate, it is accidental -- driven by chance rather than vision.
AI doesn't just add to a school's operations, it changes everything (referencing Postman's framework on technology).
Observable AI-driven changes include students outsourcing thinking, routine admin automated, and young people seeking AI for life guidance.
The Geneva vs. Broadfields fable illustrates the difference between systematic response and ad hoc reaction to environmental change.
School leaders face a binary: vision-driven, identity-grounded AI change, or being swept along by happenstance.
quotes: AI related change does not calmly knock on the front door of our school office, sign in on the school iPad and wait to be seen. It asks no permission and waits for no one.
AI has changed everything. This is how technology changes the world. It doesn't just add something, it changes everything.
Matthews' Law -- the iron law of AI change in organisations: If your AI change isn't deliberate, it's accidental.
Either our change is driven by our vision, mission, values, and purpose. Or we are swept along the stream of unconsciousness and our change is the result of chance and happenstance.
Change isn't optional, yet good change is possible.
